title: Torn Shoes (Joke)
description: This video is taken from Johari (original title: जोहारी), a 2026 short film by Subhashish Panigrahi. The film, part of the OpenSpeaks Archives, uses archival footage from the production of Panigrahi's 2021 documentary Marginalized Aadhaar. Johari features interviews with Surendra Singh Pangtey, a native Johari speaker, author, and former Indian Army and Indian Administrative Service officer. He speaks in two major forms. One form is used in highly context-specific environments, such as when two Shauka individuals on horses meet for a very brief moment as their horses cross paths. This form uses a wide set of words from the now-extinct Rankas and Shaukiya-Khun, both forms used by the tribe in the past. The other, second form is used in everyday conversation by the Shauka people, known as Johari. Chapters a. Torn Shoes (Joke) In this tiny snippet, Pangtey narrates a joke where a pun is used to narrate how a small pronunciation twist can alter a situation. He speaks in a particular form of Johari, using words from Shaukiya-Khun, a tongue now extinct.
